newsitem.title: GERMANY: German sugar industry sees higher 1996/97 output.
newsitem.headline: German sugar industry sees higher 1996/97 output.

text.p: German sugar output in the 1996/97 campaign was forecast at 3.868 million tonnes, 1.9 percent more than produced in 1995/96, sugar industry association WVZ said on Monday.
The area for the 1996/97 beet harvest was up by 0.5 percent at 516,000 hectares and the final beet yield was expected to be slightly higher this year at 5.08 tonnes per ha, WVZ said.
WVZ added that the sugar beet campaign would start early this year in mid-September, helped by good crop prospects and satisfactory demand.
It forecast a steady beet harvest volume of 26 million tonnes in 1996/97 compared with 1995/96, with a sugar content of 17 percent against an average 16.73 in 1995/96.
The third sugar beet test out of a fortnightly series of five is due to be released by WVZ on September 2.
